message.content:
### Tenant Rights in Texas (as of 2026) | Area | What You’re Entitled To | Key Points | |------|------------------------|------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Must be returned within 30 days after you move out (unless you and the landlord agree otherwise).
• Landlord may keep up to one month’s rent for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | • Landlord must provide an itemized list of deductions.
• If you disagree, you can file a claim in small‑claims court. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain the premises in a safe, livable condition (e.g., plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity). | • If the landlord fails to fix major problems, you can withhold rent *only* if the issue is serious and the landlord has been notified in writing. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑renewal or termination of a month‑to‑month lease: 30 days’ written notice.
• For a fixed‑term lease: you must give notice before the lease expires; the landlord must give notice before the lease ends. | • Written notice is required; oral notice is not sufficient. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must serve a written notice (usually 3 days for nonpayment, 30 days for lease violation).
• If you fail to comply, the landlord can file an unlawful detainer action. | • You have the right to contest the eviction in court. | | **Rent Increases** | • No statutory limit on how much a landlord can raise rent, but they must give proper notice (usually 30 days for month‑to‑month). | • For a lease, rent can only change at the end of the lease term unless both parties agree. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must give reasonable notice (usually 24 hours) before entering your unit, except in emergencies. | • “Emergency” includes fire, flood, gas leak, etc. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (including public assistance). | • This is enforced under the Texas Fair Housing Act and federal law. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major problem after notice, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from rent, but only if the problem is serious and the landlord has been notified in writing. | • Keep receipts and document the issue. | | **Lease Terms** | • All terms must be in writing if the lease is longer than one year. | • Oral agreements can be enforceable but are harder to prove. | | **Right to a Written Lease** | • Even for month‑to‑month, you can request a written lease. | • A written lease clarifies responsibilities and reduces disputes. | --- #### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Document Everything** - Keep copies of all communications (emails, texts, letters). - Take photos or videos of any damage or maintenance issues. 2. **Give Written Notice** - Use certified mail or a delivery service that provides proof of receipt. 3. **Know When to Withhold Rent** - Only do so after giving written notice and waiting the statutory period. - Consider consulting a lawyer or tenant advocacy group before withholding rent. 4. **Seek Legal Assistance** - Texas tenants can contact local tenant unions, legal aid societies, or the Texas Attorney General’s Office for guidance. - Small‑claims court is a common venue for disputes over deposits or unpaid rent. 5. **Use Online Resources** - Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA) offers guides and forms. - The Texas Legislature’s website lists statutes related to landlord‑tenant law. --- #### Quick Reference: Texas Statutes - **Texas Property Code §§ 92.001–92.021** – Security deposits. - **Texas Property Code §§ 91.001–91.021** – Habitability and repairs. - **Texas Property Code §§ 91.103–91.107** – Eviction notices. - **Texas Property Code §§ 91.201–91.207** – Lease terms and renewal. - **Texas Property Code §§ 92.001–92.021** – Discrimination protections. --- **Bottom line:** As a Texas tenant, you have the right to a safe, habitable home, timely return of your security deposit, proper notice before eviction or lease changes, and protection against discrimination. If you encounter problems, document everything, give written notice, and consider seeking legal help if needed.
